clause_evidence.reasoning: Every sample presents a scenario where the learner must actively calculate or identify a monetary total, whether by tracing a number line, selecting from options, or using an interactive visual interface. The competency action of determining value is universally tested across all 22 samples.

All samples require learners to produce or select the determined total value. Learners either type a numeric answer into a fill-in-blank field, select a correct value from multiple options, or construct an amount by manipulating visual representations. The output of a specific monetary value is required in every case across all 22 samples.

Thirteen samples directly present bills in various denominations (₱20, ₱50, ₱100, ₱200, ₱500) and require learners to determine their combined value. These span contexts from simple sums to number line movements to interactive piece selection and mixed bill-coin scenarios.

Sixteen samples present peso coins (₱1, ₱5, ₱10) or centavo coins (25¢, 50¢) and require learners to sum them. These samples encompass both coin-only contexts and mixed bill-and-coin scenarios, demonstrating competency with coin values across multiple problem types.

Ten samples explicitly mix bills and peso coins in a single problem, requiring learners to sum both types together. These combinations test the competency requirement to handle combined currency types across varied problem formats.

All 22 sample correct answers fall within the specified range, with the maximum value being exactly ₱1000 in sample 7. The smallest value is ₱2 and the largest is ₱1000, confirming that no sample exceeds the competency ceiling and the full range is represented.

Three samples present only centavo coins (25¢ and 50¢) without any peso coins or bills. Sample 5 presents four 50-centavo coins and one 25-centavo coin for a total of 225 centavos. Sample 15 presents one 50-centavo coin and one 25-centavo coin totaling 75 centavos. Sample 17 presents seven 50-centavo coins and three 25-centavo coins summing to 425 centavos. These directly test the centavo-only competency variant.

Four samples present only peso coins (₱1, ₱5, or ₱10) without centavos or bills. Sample 10 requires summing two ₱10 coins for ₱20. Sample 11 sums ₱20 and ₱5 to reach ₱25. Sample 18 adds five ₱1 coins to reach ₱5. Sample 19 adds two ₱1 coins to reach ₱2. These samples directly test competency with peso coins in isolation.

Five samples present only bills (ranging from ₱20 to ₱500) without any coins. Sample 1 uses ₱25 and three ₱50 bills reaching ₱175 on a number line. Sample 4 sums ₱200 and two ₱100 bills for ₱400. Sample 7 adds two ₱500 bills to reach ₱1000. Sample 8 sums four bills (₱500, ₱200, ₱100, ₱50) for ₱850. Sample 14 adds ₱500, three ₱50 bills, and ₱20 for ₱670. These directly test the bills-only variant.
